title: Oscillator colours
learned: Square and pulse waves sound hollow; the pulse width changes their colour
PWM moves the width all the time: a lively, chorus-like sound
The sub oscillator adds weight an octave (or two) below
Unison stacks slightly detuned copies: one oscillator sounds like many

steps.why: Before any filter, the oscillator itself has a lot of colours to offer. This lesson tours the ones that change the most.
steps.do: The notes play from SAW of the oscillator, through an open filter. Press Next.

steps.why: The square wave has only every other overtone, so it sounds hollow, like a clarinet.
steps.do: Drag a cable from SQR of the oscillator to IN of the filter (it replaces the SAW cable).
steps.after: Hollower and woodier than the saw.

steps.why: A square is high half the time. Make the high part shorter and you get a pulse wave: thinner and more nasal.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn PW of the oscillator.
steps.after: Near 50 % it is the hollow square, toward the ends a thin, reedy pulse. Every width is its own colour.

steps.why: Moving the width all the time makes the sound come alive: pulse width modulation (PWM).
steps.do: Press F2, drag a cable from TRI of the LFO to PWM of the oscillator, then press F1 and turn the PWM knob of the oscillator up.
steps.after: The tone now shimmers as if several instruments played together: the LFO sweeps the width back and forth.

steps.why: A sub oscillator plays a square one or two octaves lower. It goes into the MIX output together with the shape MORPH picks.
steps.do: Press F2 and drag a cable from MIX of the oscillator to IN of the filter. Then press F1 and turn SUB LEVEL up.
steps.after: MIX plays the shape set by MORPH (here a square), and SUB LEVEL adds the octave below: the sound gets heavier at the bottom. SUB OCT picks one or two octaves down.

steps.why: Unison runs several copies of the oscillator, each slightly out of tune with the others. Their tiny differences beat against each other and make the sound wide and thick.
steps.do: Turn VOICES of the oscillator up to 3 or more, then turn DETUNE.
steps.after: One oscillator now sounds like a whole section. A little detune is warm, a lot is the big 'supersaw' of dance music (try it with MORPH at saw).

steps.do: Wave shape, width, sub and unison: colour starts in the oscillator. Press Next to finish.
